description: Run about 2,300 customer VMs on the hypervisor clusters and storage arrays; console access; snapshots
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: 99.95% monthly SLA: about 7 hours of full outage in a month drops availability below 99.0% and triggers the 25% credit tier (about $350K); bank customers' 4-hour notification threshold (12 CFR 53.4); RPO 15 minutes applies to the paid replication tier only. Other customers' data recovery depends on their own backups per the MSA
manual_workaround: Fail replicated VMs over to DC-2; customers restore unreplicated VMs from their own backups
dependent_third_parties: DC-1 and DC-2 colocation providers; upstream carriers; hardware maintenance vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Platform engineers; NOC; DC-1 and DC-2 cages

description: Self-service provisioning, VM power and console, DNS changes, API, and tenant metering
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Running VMs keep running without the control plane, so the MTD is longer than BP-01. After a business day customers cannot scale, recover, or reach consoles, and support volume exceeds NOC capacity. RPO 1 hour limits lost orders and DNS changes; nightly backups today give only 24 hours (gap)
manual_workaround: NOC performs urgent VM power actions directly in the hypervisor managers on ticket request; DNS changes by engineer on request
dependent_third_parties: Public cloud provider; code hosting SaaS

description: Routing, firewalls, DDoS scrubbing, and authoritative DNS for customer domains
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: If DNS or routing fails, every hosted service is unreachable even though VMs are up; the same credit and bank-notification drivers as BP-01 apply. Zone data changes rarely, so a 24-hour RPO is acceptable
manual_workaround: Secondary DNS at DC-2 and at the scrubbing service; second carrier at each site

business_process: Managed services (patching, monitoring, backup) through the RMM tool
description: Remote patching, monitoring, and backup checks on about 1,900 customer servers for 58 customers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers tolerate a few days of missed patch windows; monitoring gaps longer than 3 days breach the managed services SLA. Restoring the RMM tool after a compromise needs integrity checks first (see P08), so speed is not the priority
manual_workaround: Engineers log in to critical customer servers through the customers' own remote access; patching deferred

description: Ticketing, phone line, status page, and incident communication to customers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: During any platform incident customers must reach the NOC and see status; bank customers need notice when an incident may pass 4 hours. Loss of the ticketing system during an outage multiplies reputational harm
manual_workaround: Status page hosted by a separate provider; NOC cell phones and a published backup phone number; shared mailbox
dependent_third_parties: Ticketing SaaS; status page provider; phone carrier
dependent_people_or_facilities: NOC staff; Florida HQ (NOC can work remotely)

description: Build and release the control plane and portal; build and sign VM templates
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Releases can wait a few days. Security fixes cannot wait longer than the vulnerability timeframes the company adopts (see P03 VDR rows). Git history is distributed across engineers' clones
manual_workaround: Emergency fixes built from a clean engineer workstation under two-person review

mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: An incident during a SIEM outage could go unseen; the P08 runbook depends on SIEM data; logs lost beyond 1 hour weaken the evidence trail
manual_workaround: EDR console alerts go directly to IT on-call; cloud provider native alerts

description: Usage metering export, invoicing, card and ACH collection
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Monthly invoicing cycle; about $2.0M billed per month; a 10-day delay is absorbable with the credit line
manual_workaround: Invoice from the prior month's usage and true up later

description: Quotes, contracts, customer onboarding, federal and bank due-diligence responses
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Pipeline can pause for a week; due-diligence deadlines from banks and the prospective agency sponsor are usually 2 to 4 weeks
manual_workaround: Work from email and the productivity suite

mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Biweekly payroll; a missed payroll has legal and retention impact; terminations must still remove access the same day
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider; IT removes access from HR email
